WP27_BustleArmor.question: Three scallops vs irregular 2D contour

evidence.1000: In current wp27 1000-right versus r4 1000-right, the smooth W-shaped lobes are replaced by an irregular, broken lower contour. However, the three dark vertical columns remain at the same evenly spaced positions (about x 150, 270 and 400), so the threefold periodicity still dominates. Current 1000-front-three-quarter shows the same left face, with three equally spaced dark columns, softened but still present. 1000-top shows the cavity and bores unchanged, and the stair-stepped crescent shading in the bores persists (minor).
evidence.256: In current 256-right versus r4 256-right, the three faint columns are nearly identical. The contour improvement does not survive at this size.
evidence.128: In current 128-right, the pattern is lost (part-scale only).

WP27_BustleArmor.objection: The equal spacing of the three char columns still reads as a projection or mask artifact. The irregular contour fixed the edge but not the rhythm.

WP23_P23_BlowoffRight.question: Trim

evidence.1000: In current 1000-top versus r4 1000-top, the trim changed from a light mid-gray outline to dark charcoal that matches the charred field. The prior objection (a clean protected rim inside the fire field) is resolved. In 1000-front-three-quarter, the trim is dark on all sides apart from a thin lit thickness edge at the lower left. In 1000-front, the end caps are dark squares.
evidence.256: In current 256-top, there is no light outline. Compare r4 256-front-three-quarter, where the lighter rim was visible.
evidence.128: In current 128-front-three-quarter, the plate reads as a dark plate, and only a faint lit edge at the lower left remains.

WP23_P23_BlowoffRight.limits: The panel interior is still a smooth airbrushed lateral gradient with faint vertical banding steps (1000-top, about x 250–290 and x 470). The dark trim now frames the tan left zone, a mild reverse emphasis. These are acceptable only within the whole-field breakup scope already noted.

WP29_RightStowage.question: Floor versus walls

evidence.1000: In current 1000-top versus r4 1000-top, the floor is lifted from near-black to dark gray, with a faint lighter rim and corner highlight. In current 1000-front-three-quarter versus r4 1000-front-three-quarter, the visible floor patch near the tear (about x 250–350, y 355–400) is now distinguishably lighter than the walls. In current 1000-rear-three-quarter versus r4, the view is visually unchanged: tan exterior to black interior is still a hard value step at the torn rim, and the mounting blocks are pure black.
evidence.256: In current 256-top, the floor still reads as a uniform dark slab.
evidence.128: In current 128-right, the black zig-zag graphic band persists at part scale. In whole 1000-right, the same graphic is unchanged.

WP29_RightStowage.objection: The floor and wall separation exists at 1000 only and is weak. It is still dark gray, not a distinctly lighter matte residue role. The exterior rim step, the main cause of the whole-model zig-zag graphic, was not addressed.

WP82_Surface.question: Perimeter edge

evidence.1000: In current 1000-front-three-quarter versus r5 standalone, the left long edge changed from near-black to dark gray, so the perimeter is more uniform. In current 1000-front versus r5, the fold edge is now a lighter gray, giving more of a cut-edge cue, but it still switches against the darker left flat segment. In current 1000-left versus r5, the rightmost flat edge segment is still much darker than the middle segment.
evidence.256: In current 256-left, the gray/dark segment switch is still visible.
evidence.128: In current 128-front-three-quarter, it reads as a dark fragment with a uniform-looking rim, and the switching is not legible.

WP82_Surface.objection: Per-face value switching is reduced but still present. I cannot separate albedo from face-orientation lighting in these captures. I do not recommend another charged finish pass on this part until an unlit or albedo control shows whether the remaining switching is authored.

WP30_RearBasket.question: Cast-shadow stripe

evidence.1000: Current 1000-front is visually identical to r4 1000-front, including the dark diagonal mark on the middle rail at the right end post (about x 900–930, y 495–505) and the small ticks at the top right. Current 1000-front-three-quarter shows a uniform charcoal lattice.
evidence.256: In current 256-front, there is a faint tick at the right end of the middle rail. It is near sub-pixel.

WP30_RearBasket.shadowNote: I accept the presentation-effect attribution as previously proven, per the brief. I did not open the control myself. Consistent with that, the mark is unchanged from r4 under the same rig.
WP30_RearBasket.limits: There is no heat or value variation, so the rack reads as black-painted as easily as burnt. This is unchanged and accepted.
